sections.heading: What is vowel harmony?
paragraphs: Vowel harmony is a key feature of Hungarian. It means that suffixes (such as endings or postpositions) change depending on the vowels in the word.
Hungarian vowels are divided into three groups: front, back, and mixed.

rows: a, á, o, ó, u, ú
e, é, i, í, ö, ő, ü, ű

sections.heading: Suffix harmony examples
paragraphs: Most Hungarian suffixes have a back-vowel and a front-vowel version. You choose the one that matches the word’s vowel type.

sections.heading: Important points
list: Suffixes must match the vowel type of the word they follow.
If a word has both front and back vowels (mixed), the last vowel usually decides.
Some foreign words or exceptions break this rule — these must be learned separately.

sections.heading: Examples
list: A házban lakom. – I live in the house.
A boltban vásárolok. – I shop in the store.
A könyvben sok kép van. – There are many pictures in the book.
A tükörrel nézem magam. – I look at myself with the mirror.
